transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi… thanks for seeing me. I guess, um, work kind of pushed me to come in. I’ve been having trouble keeping up with scheduled callbacks and work orders, and sometimes even just basic follow-ups I told people I’d do. I don’t mean to drop things, it just keeps happening, and it’s gotten pretty piled up.

I’m trying to handle it, but they’re worried, and honestly I’m worried too… especially because I was hoping to move up, and I don’t want this to ruin that chance.
Have you had trouble with attention or staying organized like this since you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I was a terrible student or anything—I did okay in some ways, and teachers would say I was bright—but even back in grade school I was kind of… scattered.

I remember misplacing papers a lot, missing parts of directions, and needing reminders to finish classwork. So I guess it’s not totally new with this job pressure. It’s just more noticeable now, if that makes sense.
Outside of work, do these kinds of attention and organization problems also interfere with your daily life?

Um… outside of work, I guess I notice it, but the thing that’s really gotten bad is the work side of it. Like, the scheduled callbacks, work orders, and follow-ups I said I’d do… they just kept slipping, and now it’s piled up enough that they wanted me to come talk to someone.

I don’t want it to sound like I don’t care, because I really do. I’m trying. But it’s gotten to the point where I’m scared it’s going to mess up my chance to move up, if that makes sense.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like, unusually energized or not needing sleep. I mean, I’ve had times where I’m stressed and don’t sleep great, but I wouldn’t say I felt like I had all this extra energy or anything. Is that what you mean?
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days lately?

I don’t think so… not most days. I mean, I get frustrated with myself and kind of discouraged when I’m behind or I feel like I’m letting people down, but I wouldn’t say I’m depressed most of the time. At least, I don’t think that’s the main thing.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about many different things?

Um… I worry some, sure, but I don’t know if I’d say it’s a lot about everything. Mostly it’s when I’m behind or I think I might have messed something up. I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is, though. Is that the kind of worrying you mean?
How often do you drink alcohol?

Um… I don’t really know how to answer exactly. I mean, I’ll have a drink sometimes, like socially or after work once in a while, but I wouldn’t say it’s a big thing. Not every day or anything. Is that what you’re asking?
Do you also have these kinds of forgetfulness or organization problems at home?

Yeah… I mean, at home too, but the bigger problem has really been at work. I keep missing scheduled callbacks, forgetting work orders, or not following up when I told someone I would. I feel bad saying it because I really do try, but it’s piled up enough that work wanted me to come in before I mess up my chance to move up. Does that make sense?
Did these problems get noticeably worse after a particular stressful event?

I don’t think it was like one stressful personal event, exactly. It’s been more… since the new management company took over and changed our department to digital work orders and tighter documentation. That was about 11 months ago, and that’s when it started being more noticeable. I mean, I probably could’ve adjusted better, but that’s when it got worse, I guess.
Since the switch to digital work orders, have you been feeling emotionally upset about that change?

I don’t think emotionally upset is exactly how I’d put it. I mean, it’s frustrating, sure, and I don’t like feeling like I’m messing things up, but I haven’t been sitting around, like… devastated about the system change or anything. It’s more that I’m having trouble keeping up with it. Does that make sense?
